notes_on_narrative: The 10-K is structurally generic about DoD exposure: ATI is a specialty materials supplier (titanium, nickel alloys, zirconium, hafnium, niobium) selling INTO defense end-markets via primes (Boeing, GE Aviation/Safran, Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney). The filing does NOT name specific Pentagon Program Elements (PE numbers) or specific named DoD programs (no Skyborg, no CCA, no SDA Tracking Layer, no Sentinel/GBSD, no Columbia, no Virginia-class, no F-35/F-47 by name in narrative text). It cites broad applications: 'naval nuclear products, military jet engines, fixed wing and rotorcraft products, armor applications and munitions materials.' This pattern of GENERIC defense exposure (specialty materials sold to many programs) is structurally different from the J-Book divergence target pattern (small-cap claims a specific PE drives revenue; J-Book shows PE zeroed). Most claims here will resolve NOT_FOUND in pentagon_jbook (correct UNVERIFIABLE outcome for a broad materials supplier).

claims.claim_text: Aerospace & defense end markets represent approximately 68% of total ATI sales in FY 2025.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.source_quote: Aerospace & defense, our largest end markets, represent approximately 68% of total sales, led by products for jet engines and airframes in addition to a wide range of defense applications.

claims.claim_text: Defense product sales grew 14% in FY 2025 across ATI and 24% in HPMC; ATI expects continued growth in the defense end market in coming years.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.object_value: FY25 +14% defense; HPMC defense +24%; expects continued growth
claims.source_quote: In fiscal year 2025, sales to our defense end market increased by 14% and we expect continued growth in this important end market in the coming years... HPMC has also experienced strong growth in defense products, with fiscal year 2025 sales growth of 24%.

claims.claim_text: ATI produces materials and components for naval nuclear products, a forward-funded DoD/DOE area.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.object_value: naval nuclear products (zirconium, hafnium, specialty alloys)
claims.source_quote: Our materials and components are used for many applications, including naval nuclear products, military jet engines, fixed wing and rotorcraft products, armor applications and munitions materials.

claims.claim_text: ATI has a long-term agreement (LTA) with Boeing covering value-added titanium products for aircraft airframes and structural components.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.source_quote: long-term supply agreement for aircraft airframes and structural components with Boeing. This LTA covers value-added titanium products...

claims.claim_text: ATI has LTAs with GE Aviation and Safran for premium titanium alloys, nickel-based alloys and components for commercial and military jet engines.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.object_value: GE Aviation + Safran LTAs for jet engine alloys (commercial + military)
claims.source_quote: we have LTAs with several aircraft engine manufacturers, including GE Aviation and Safran, to supply premium titanium alloys, nickel-based alloys and components for commercial and military jet engine applications.

claims.claim_text: ATI has LTAs with Rolls-Royce plc and Pratt & Whitney for forgings and disc-quality mill products for jet engines.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.object_value: Rolls-Royce + Pratt & Whitney engine forging LTAs
claims.source_quote: we have LTAs with Rolls-Royce plc for the supply of disc-quality mill products and precision forgings for commercial jet engine applications and with Pratt & Whitney to provide isothermal and conventional forgings

claims.claim_text: ATI is positioned to capture multi-year demand growth from current and next-generation jet engines and airframes via long-term supply agreements and a fully qualified asset base.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.object_value: well-positioned for multi-year next-generation jet engine + airframe demand
claims.source_quote: we believe that through alloy development, internal growth efforts, and long-term supply agreements on current and next-generation jet engines and airframes, we are well-positioned with a fully qualified asset base to meet the expected multi-year demand growth

claims.claim_text: ATI HPMC operates an additive manufacturing facility in Margate, FL that serves the aerospace & defense industries with laser powder bed fusion parts.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.source_quote: we lease a facility in Margate, Florida to perform metal alloy-based additive manufacturing for the aerospace & defense industries... ATI also has a dedicated additive manufacturing and post-processing facility to tap into significant aerospace & defense demand for additively manufactured laser powered bed fusion parts

claims.claim_text: ATI maintains owned and operated facilities for nickel/titanium/zirconium/hafnium melting and processing across NC, OR, AL, NY, PA, SC, WA, WI and CA — all substantially owned and active per the 10-K.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.object_value: domestic specialty materials footprint (PA, NC, OR, AL, NY, SC, WA, WI, CA)
claims.source_quote: Domestic melting operations are located in Monroe and Bakers, NC, and Richland, WA... Our production of zirconium, hafnium, niobium and related specialty alloys takes place at facilities located in Millersburg, OR and Huntsville, AL. Nickel melting operations are located in Lockport, NY... titanium melting operations are located in Albany, OR... Brackenridge and Latrobe, PA.

claims.claim_text: ATI grew specialty energy / naval nuclear-adjacent specialty materials revenue alongside aerospace & defense; zirconium/hafnium are used in nuclear power and naval nuclear applications.
claims.subject: ATI
claims.object_value: zirconium/hafnium for nuclear power + naval nuclear
claims.source_quote: AA&S produces nickel-based alloys, titanium and titanium-based alloys, and specialty alloys, including zirconium, hafnium, and niobium... AA&S focuses on high-value materials that are utilized in technically challenging and extreme environments, which require materials that can withstand extreme heat, radiation and corrosion.
